{{short description|American mathematician}}
'''David Kent Harrison''' (April 6, 1931, Massachusetts – December 21, 1999, [[Barnstable, Massachusetts]]) was an American mathematician, specializing in [[algebra]], particularly [[homological algebra]] and [[valuation theory]].

He completed his PhD at [[Princeton University]] in 1957; his dissertation, titled ''On torsion free abelian groups'', was written under the supervision of [[Emil Artin]].<ref name=MathGen>{{MathGenealogy|id=12418}}</ref>

Harrison was a faculty member from 1959 to 1963 at the [[University of Pennsylvania]]<ref>{{cite web|title=Faculty History|website=Department of Mathematics, University of Pennsylvania|url=http://www.math.upenn.edu/about/department-history/faculty-history}}</ref> and from 1963 to 1993 at the [[University of Oregon]], retiring there as professor emeritus in 1993.<ref name=UOregon>{{cite web|title=Former Faculty|website=Department of Mathematics, University of Oregon|url=http://math.uoregon.edu/people/former-faculty}}</ref>

He developed a commutative [[cohomology]] theory for [[commutative algebra (structure)|commutative algebras]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Harrison |first1=D. K. |title=Commutative Algebras and Cohomology |journal=Transactions of the American Mathematical Society |date=1962 |volume=104| issue=2 |pages=191–204 |mr=0142607 |doi=10.1090/S0002-9947-1962-0142607-6 |url=https://www.ams.org/journals/tran/1962-104-02/S0002-9947-1962-0142607-6/home.html |accessdate=April 3, 2020|doi-access=free |url-access=subscription }}</ref> Along with his colleague [[Marie A. Vitulli]], he developed a unified valuation theory for [[ring (mathematics)|ring]]s with [[zero divisor]]s that generalized both Krull and Archimedean valuations.<ref name="v-valn">{{cite journal |last1=Harrison |first1=D. K. |last2=Vitulli |first2=Marie A. |title=V-Valuations of a Commutative Ring I |journal=J. Algebra |date=1989 |volume=65 |issue=3 |pages=264–292 |mr=1024992| doi=10.1016/0021-8693(89)90305-0 |doi-access=free }}</ref>

He was a [[Guggenheim Fellow]] for the academic year 1963–1964.<ref>{{cite web|title=David Kent Harrison|website=John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation|url=https://www.gf.org/fellows/all-fellows/david-kent-harrison/|access-date=August 14, 2018|archive-date=August 15, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180815024342/https://www.gf.org/fellows/all-fellows/david-kent-harrison/|url-status=dead}}</ref> He supervised 28 doctoral students including [[Joel Cunningham]].<ref name=MathGen/> Ann Hill Harrison endowed the Harrison Memory Award for outstanding mathematical students at the University of Oregon.<ref name=UOregon/> He is survived by his son, composer and pianist [[Michael Harrison (musician)|Michael Harrison]], a [[Guggenheim Fellow]] for the academic year 2018–2019,<ref>{{cite web|title=Michael Harrison|website=John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation|url=https://www.gf.org/fellows/all-fellows/michael-harrison/|access-date=June 6, 2019|archive-date=June 7, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190607003309/https://www.gf.org/fellows/all-fellows/michael-harrison/|url-status=dead}}</ref> and his daughter Jo Ellen Harrison.
